question: Should experimental Claws be permitted to register arbitrary package-declared stdio MCP commands and share exact global `mcp.servers` entries, or must both capabilities be brokered and explicitly host-authorized?
rationale: The correct boundary determines whether this is an acceptable extension of existing MCP configuration or an execution and cross-agent authorization escalation; the patch cannot safely choose that product-security policy on its own.

options.title: Broker commands and authorize sharing
options.body: Require trusted or brokered stdio command identities and an explicit host approval for cross-Claw/global MCP reuse before this lifecycle slice can merge.

options.title: Restrict the first experimental scope
options.body: Limit this slice to a narrower MCP declaration class that does not introduce package-controlled local execution or implicit global sharing.

options.title: Pause the MCP slice
options.body: Defer this ownership feature until the Claws RFC specifies the permanent execution and shared-resource authorization model.

recommendation.title: Broker commands and authorize sharing
recommendation.body: Require trusted or brokered stdio command identities and an explicit host approval for cross-Claw/global MCP reuse before this lifecycle slice can merge.
